evaluated.name: Durable Margin Sales Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Low price-to-sales firms outperform when their sales carry high, persistent gross margins rather than weak or unstable economics.
evaluated.reasoning: The numerator rewards average gross margin and penalizes margin volatility, while the denominator measures the market price paid per unit of sales. Industry ranking makes the quality-adjusted sales valuation comparable among firms with similar production economics.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Retained Profit Accumulation Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to their sustained accumulation of internally generated equity earn stronger subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The signal replaces the static retained-earnings sign screen with a continuous flow measure of additions to retained capital, normalized directly by market value. Averaging changes over three periods reduces one-year accounting noise while distinguishing internal compounders from firms consuming accumulated equity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Self-Financed EBITDA Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt-inclusive EBITDA bargains outperform when operating earnings are not accompanied by growth in total liabilities.
evaluated.reasoning: Liability accumulation is subtracted from smoothed EBITDA, penalizing firms whose apparent operating performance depends on supplier credit, accruals, acquisitions, or other new claims. Declining liabilities increase the conservative earnings numerator, identifying cheap firms that are simultaneously generating earnings and repairing their financing structure.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Maintenance-Reserve Cash Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to cash flow remaining after a depreciation-based replacement reserve earn stronger subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Unadjusted operating cash flow can make capital-intensive or deteriorating firms appear deceptively cheap because depreciation is added back despite recurring replacement needs. Subtracting smoothed depreciation produces a conservative cash-earnings yield intended to separate distributable cash generation from capital-consumption value traps.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Earned-Cash Discount
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash balances are supported by accumulated internal profitability.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash-to-market identifies liquid-asset cheapness, while the retained-earnings share distinguishes earned cash from liquidity raised through external financing. Unlike multiplying two potentially zero-centered ranks, the nonnegative cash-yield leg scales a signed quality state, so accumulated deficits reduce rather than invert the signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Through-Cycle Margin Floor Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to sales outperform when even their recent worst-case gross margin indicates resilient unit economics.
evaluated.reasoning: The historical margin floor converts current sales into a conservative through-cycle gross-profit capacity rather than reproducing current gross-profits-to-market. Because sales yield is generally nonnegative, a weak or negative margin floor lowers the signal without the sign inversion created by multiplying two centered ranks.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Claim-Covered Dividend Value
evaluated.hypothesis: High dividend-yield firms outperform when recurring operating cash flow provides strong coverage of short-term liability claims.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces retained-profit accumulation with a payout-sustainability mechanism linking market yield to cash coverage of near-term obligations. Dividend payers with negative operating cash flow receive negative scores, while zero-dividend firms remain neutral rather than being mixed into the distressed short tail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Liquidity-Recovery Book Bargain
evaluated.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms outperform when their net liquid-asset position is improving relative to total assets.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike the static net-net ratio, this signal uses book value for valuation and the trajectory of normalized liquidity as a separate quality state. The weak-link interaction requires both a genuine book discount and balance-sheet recovery, reducing exposure to firms that remain cheap because liquidity continues to deteriorate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Depreciation-Reconciled Earnings Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms are more likely to be genuine earnings-value bargains when the cash-versus-income difference is largely explained by depreciation rather than other accrual movements.
evaluated.reasoning: Depreciation is an expected noncash source of the operating-cash-flow and income gap; the remaining absolute residual captures less transparent working-capital and accrual effects. Subtracting that residual from smoothed earnings produces a conservative yield that rewards both cheapness and accounting reconciliation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Downside-Covered Operating Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Debt-inclusive EBITDA bargains outperform when operating cash flow has consistently covered current liabilities even in the weakest recent period.
evaluated.reasoning: The minimum historical cash-coverage ratio measures downside solvency rather than average profitability, helping exclude firms whose current valuation reflects episodic funding stress. The weak-link interaction requires both operating cheapness and robust claim coverage, which should produce cleaner long and short portfolio tails.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Working-Capital-Release-Adjusted Cash Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating cash flow after removing cash generated through working-capital liquidation earn stronger subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The positive-part adjustment subtracts only declines in noncash working capital that temporarily boost operating cash flow; it does not add back working-capital investment. This asymmetric treatment is conservative and avoids reconstructing the conventional cash-flow-to-price numerator.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Liability-Productivity Sales Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when operating earnings generated per dollar of liabilities are improving.
evaluated.reasoning: The quality mechanism is creditor productivity rather than an arbitrarily weighted penalty for liability growth. Because sales yield is generally nonnegative, deterioration in EBITDA per liability lowers the signal directly, while improving liability productivity amplifies cheap sales without combining mismatched quantities additively.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Enterprise Earned-Cash Discount
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash is more likely to be undervalued when it is inexpensive relative to total capital claims and supported by accumulated internal profitability.
evaluated.reasoning: This retains enterprise scaling to reduce concentration in small, levered cash-rich firms but replaces the empirically weak operating-cash-flow-to-current-liabilities leg with the better-supported retained-earnings quality state. The cash ratio is nonnegative, so accumulated deficits intentionally reduce the score rather than creating a flow-driven sign inversion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Historically Restored Margin Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Low price-to-sales firms outperform when gross margins are both economically strong and near the top of the firm’s own recent history.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the generic book-value-plus-improving-profitability construction with a firm-specific margin-restoration mechanism. The nested weak-link interaction requires cheap sales, a strong margin level, and a favorable within-firm margin position, preventing any single textbook value or quality leg from dominating.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Dual-Reserve Distributable Cash Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to cash remaining after both a replacement reserve and any working-capital liquidation benefit earn stronger subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Maintenance-adjusted cash flow and release-adjusted cash flow separately produced the strongest portfolio evidence in prior generations. This construction requires cash to survive both adjustments, targeting genuinely distributable operating cash rather than combining the two signals as separate ranked anomalies.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Claim-Adjusted Liability Productivity
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales relative to total capital claims outperform when EBITDA generated per dollar of liabilities is improving.
evaluated.reasoning: Liability-productivity sales value produced reliable portfolio alpha but a weaker cross-sectional slope, potentially because market-cap scaling made highly levered firms appear excessively cheap. Including total liabilities in the valuation denominator retains the operational-improvement mechanism while requiring cheapness relative to all claims.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Maintenance Cash Runway Discount
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms outperform when their cash discount is not offset by an ongoing maintenance-adjusted operating cash burn.
evaluated.reasoning: The quality penalty activates only when operating cash flow after depreciation is negative, so profitable firms retain an ordinary cash-value interpretation while cash-burning firms receive a continuous runway penalty. This asymmetric denominator avoids multiplying cash value by a signed flow and directly targets cash-rich value traps.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rising-Claims Asset Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to assets underperform when a rising share of those assets is financed by liabilities.
evaluated.reasoning: Assets-to-market is often elevated precisely because equity value has collapsed under creditor pressure; here that leverage sensitivity is used deliberately to identify traps rather than treated as genuine cheapness. The nonnegative asset-value leg amplifies a signed deterioration in the liability ratio, producing a directly interpretable negative-return signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Refinancing-Relief Cash Discount
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when the proportion of liabilities requiring near-term settlement is declining.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the familiar cash-to-price × profitability composite with a liability-maturity mechanism: cash becomes more plausibly available to shareholders as refinancing pressure recedes. The cash-yield leg is nonnegative, so a rising current-liability share produces an intentionally negative score rather than an accidental sign inversion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Maintenance-Confirmed Sales Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when those sales generate positive cash profitability after a depreciation-based replacement reserve.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the gross-margin family that produced strong cross-sectional slopes but no portfolio alpha and instead uses the empirically stronger maintenance-cash mechanism as the quality test. Ranking the two legs separately eliminates the scale mismatch, while the weak-link interaction prevents cheap sales from compensating for poor distributable cash generation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash discount is not offset by a cumulative retained-earnings deficit.
evaluated.reasoning: Unlike cash-to-price multiplied by a generic profitability rank, this construction treats accumulated losses as a stock claim against the apparent cash surplus. The asymmetric penalty leaves positive-retained-earnings firms on a normal cash-value scale while continuously demoting cash-rich firms with deep historical deficits.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Idle-Asset Value Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Asset-cheap firms underperform when sales generated per dollar of current assets are persistently declining.
evaluated.reasoning: The severe portfolio failure of liquidity-recovery book value suggests that apparent balance-sheet improvement can reflect contraction or idle-asset accumulation rather than genuine quality. This signal deliberately identifies that trap by combining asset cheapness with deteriorating current-asset productivity instead of rewarding liquidity growth itself.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Operating-Asset-Liquidation-Adjusted Cash Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating cash flow after removing proceeds from noncash current-asset liquidation earn stronger subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Declines in noncash current assets, unlike generic increases in current liabilities, represent operating working-capital releases that directly elevate operating cash flow. The one-sided haircut therefore removes an identifiable liquidation benefit without incorrectly treating short-term borrowing as an operating inflow.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash-Bounded Operating Claim Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to conservatively cash-realizable operating earnings earn stronger subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The lower of smoothed EBITDA and operating cash flow prevents reported operating earnings from exceeding their cash realization while giving no extra reward when cash flow temporarily exceeds EBITDA. Both numerator inputs are flows and the denominator is a stock of equity and liability claims, eliminating the prior flow-stock adjustment mismatch.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Retained-Earnings Rollforward Value
evaluated.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms earn stronger subsequent returns when reported income reconciles with additions to retained earnings plus common dividends.
evaluated.reasoning: The retained-earnings rollforward provides an accounting-identity quality check rather than another profitability level or growth signal. Subtracting the absolute unexplained residual from earnings penalizes cheap firms affected by restatements, direct-to-equity adjustments, or other opaque reconciliation items; unreported dividends are treated as zero.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Capital-Consumption Asset Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to assets underperform when depreciation expense is rising persistently relative to sales.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the repeated maintenance-cash-burn aggregation with a deterioration mechanism linking asset cheapness to increasing capital consumption per revenue dollar. The nonnegative asset-value leg amplifies a signed depreciation-intensity trend, identifying assets that may look cheap because their productive economics are worsening.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Accrual-Bounded Cash Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to the lower of operating cash flow and accrual-implied cash earnings earn stronger subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Income plus depreciation provides an accrual-based cash-earnings benchmark, while reported operating cash flow captures realized cash generation. Taking the lower value prevents temporary working-capital releases from inflating the signal without requiring the sparse current-asset-change data used by earlier liquidation adjustments.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Accrual-Opacity Asset Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Asset-cheap firms underperform when the cash-versus-income gap contains a large component not explained by depreciation.
evaluated.reasoning: The prior reconciliation signal may have diluted the effect by subtracting opacity from a positive earnings yield across the full distribution. This trap-side construction instead concentrates directly on cheap assets with large absolute non-depreciation accrual residuals, creating a clean negative-return hypothesis without signed-accrual inversions.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Signed Deficit-Adjusted Cash Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Positive operating cash flow predicts stronger returns when it is inexpensive and not undermined by accumulated deficits, while negative operating cash flow remains an unambiguously adverse signal.
evaluated.reasoning: The expression separates positive and negative cash-flow branches: deficits enlarge the denominator only for positive cash flow, while negative cash flow enters as an explicitly negative yield. This removes the prior sign reversal that made deficit-laden cash burners appear less negative and therefore artificially better ranked.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Noncash-Asset Liquidation Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms generating large noncash current-asset liquidations relative to market value earn weaker subsequent returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the declining-productivity template and directly measures the liquidation source that earlier conservative cash-yield signals successfully removed from operating cash flow. Scaling the one-sided liquidation amount by market value targets firms whose apparent cheapness depends materially on selling down receivables, inventory, or other operating current assets.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Short-Term Funding Sales Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to sales underperform when current liabilities are rising persistently relative to the operating costs they support.
evaluated.reasoning: Current liabilities are evaluated relative to cost of goods sold rather than treated as a direct offset to cash holdings, distinguishing operating funding pressure from a static cash anomaly. The nonnegative sales-yield leg amplifies a signed deterioration in short-term funding intensity without relying on unstable operating-cash-flow coverage.

evaluated.name: Deficit-Burden Sales Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that look inexpensive relative to sales underperform when accumulated losses represent a large share of their asset base.
evaluated.reasoning: Both legs are nonnegative, so deeper accumulated deficits always strengthen the trap signal and cannot improve the ranking when another component is adverse. This uses the empirically successful deficit mechanism on the trap side, identifying cheap revenue bases lacking evidence of cumulative shareholder value creation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Continuous Maintenance Sales Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when those sales support positive maintenance-adjusted cash profitability.
evaluated.reasoning: The earlier MIN combination of these channels produced a poor long-short portfolio because any weak leg pushed heterogeneous firms into the short tail. This continuous interaction instead makes cash-burning firms explicitly negative and scales positive maintenance profitability by sales cheapness, preserving economically ordered tails.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: EBITDA Cash-Conversion Sales Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that look inexpensive relative to sales underperform when EBITDA materially exceeds operating cash flow relative to their operating cost base.
evaluated.reasoning: A positive EBITDA-to-cash shortfall identifies operating earnings that have not been realized in cash, while the one-sided operator avoids penalizing firms whose cash flow exceeds EBITDA. Scaling the shortfall by cost of goods sold makes the quality defect comparable across firms before sales cheapness magnifies it.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: EBITDA-Cash Concordance Claim Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating earnings earn stronger subsequent returns when EBITDA and operating cash flow are closely aligned.
evaluated.reasoning: The prior lower-bound claim yield penalized only cash flow below EBITDA, even though unusually high cash flow can also reflect temporary working-capital liquidation. Subtracting the absolute EBITDA-cash gap creates a symmetric realization penalty while keeping the numerator in dollar flows and the denominator in total equity and liability claims.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Working-Asset Cash Productivity Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when their current-asset base generates high operating cash flow.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the accumulated-deficit cash-stock construction with an operating-efficiency mechanism linking sales valuation to cash productivity. The nonnegative sales-yield leg scales a signed cash-return measure, so cash-consuming firms receive negative scores rather than benefiting from a denominator adjustment.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash-Conversion Instability Sales Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to sales underperform when conversion of gross profit into operating cash flow is unstable.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons working-capital growth and instead measures second-moment instability in the realization of gross profit as cash. High values require both apparent sales cheapness and unreliable cash conversion, targeting a specific trap tail rather than repackaging declining asset turnover.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Accelerating Funding-Pressure Sales Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales underperform when current liabilities relative to operating costs are increasing at an accelerating rate.
evaluated.reasoning: Acceleration is signed: worsening funding pressure raises the signal, while decelerating or reversing pressure lowers it, restoring the intended negative-return ordering that the nonnegative historical-rank leg lacked. It tests whether the strongest funding-pressure anomaly is concentrated in firms where short-term financing stress is intensifying rather than merely elevated.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Deficit-adjusted cash bargains earn stronger subsequent returns when current-asset productivity is also improving.
evaluated.reasoning: The accumulated-deficit cash ratio supplies the strongest broad-coverage value evidence, while improving sales per current asset distinguishes productive liquidity from idle cash accumulation. Using separate ranked channels avoids sign reversals and does not mechanically multiply cash value by a potentially negative quality state.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Funding-Safe Maintenance Sales Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Maintenance-cash-supported sales bargains earn stronger returns when short-term funding pressure is easing rather than intensifying.
evaluated.reasoning: Continuous maintenance sales value generated coherent slope and portfolio evidence, while rising current liabilities relative to costs reliably identified the opposite trap tail. The ranked composite preserves both effects on comparable scales without multiplying two signed quantities or allowing worsening funding pressure to improve the score.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Maintenance-Productive Cash Discount
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when ongoing operations generate positive cash profitability after a depreciation-based replacement reserve.
evaluated.reasoning: The cash-yield leg is nonnegative, so maintenance cash profitability determines the signal’s direction without sign inversion: cash-burning firms receive negative scores and productive firms positive scores. This tests whether the strong cash-discount and maintenance-cash mechanisms reinforce one another continuously rather than only through a distress-only denominator penalty.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms underperform when growth in current liabilities exceeds operating cash generation by a large amount relative to market value.
evaluated.reasoning: This measures a single funding-shortfall mechanism rather than averaging separate productivity and funding-pressure signals. The liability change and operating cash flow are both dollar flows, while market-value scaling makes the uncovered claim growth most consequential among apparently cheap firms.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Through-Cycle Depreciation-Covered EBITDA Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to EBITDA earn stronger subsequent returns when operating earnings cover a conservative through-cycle depreciation burden.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the liability-productivity substitution with a capital-consumption mechanism: recent peak depreciation serves as a conservative reserve against overstated operating earning power. Firms whose smoothed EBITDA cannot cover that reserve receive low or negative yields, reducing exposure to capital-intensive value traps.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Cash-Covered Conservative Claim Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms earn stronger subsequent returns when conservatively cash-realizable operating earnings are inexpensive relative to equity value plus liabilities not covered by cash.
evaluated.reasoning: Cash modifies the economic claim base directly rather than entering as a separately ranked value signal, while the lower-bound numerator prevents EBITDA from exceeding its cash realization. The nonnegative unfunded-liability term avoids negative-enterprise-value distortions and represents the obligations that remain after available cash coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Deficit-adjusted cash bargains earn stronger subsequent returns when current liabilities are declining relative to the operating costs they finance.
evaluated.reasoning: Rising short-term funding intensity generated strong negative cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, making its reversal an economically supported quality state rather than an untested screen. The construction combines the cash-value level with standalone funding relief, avoiding duplication of a common price-scaled value leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Liability-Origin-Adjusted Cash Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash balances are not explained by recent growth in liability financing.
evaluated.reasoning: This tests cash provenance rather than combining cash value with another profitability measure: positive liability growth is treated as an external source that reduces the cash plausibly generated for shareholders. The cash stock and liability change are both dollar quantities, and cash raised without liability expansion retains its full valuation weight.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Through-Cycle Solvency Sales Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to sales earn stronger subsequent returns when current assets have consistently covered total liabilities.
evaluated.reasoning: The quality mechanism is a through-cycle uncovered-liability stock rather than another profitability or turnover trend. Because sales are generally nonnegative, adding the recent maximum solvency shortfall to the valuation denominator cannot create the sign reversal that occurs when denominator penalties are applied to negative earnings.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Deteriorating Cash-Conversion Sales Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to sales underperform when conversion of gross profit into operating cash flow is persistently deteriorating.
evaluated.reasoning: This targets a signed change in cash realization rather than substituting one accounting denominator inside an existing productivity formula. The nonnegative sales-yield leg magnifies worsening cash conversion among cheap firms, while improving conversion produces a negative trap score.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Double-Funding Distress Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms underperform when they simultaneously increase current liabilities and liquidate noncash current assets by amounts large relative to market value.
evaluated.reasoning: The minimum of the two positive-part flows requires both forms of emergency funding rather than allowing either generic working-capital movement to dominate. This identifies firms raising short-term claims while also consuming receivables, inventory, or other operating liquidity—a sharper distress mechanism than a depreciation tweak to cash-flow coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Working-Capital-Reserved Gross Profit Yield
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to gross profit earn stronger subsequent returns when that profit does not require a large working-capital adjustment.
evaluated.reasoning: Gross profit is reduced by the absolute dollar movement in noncash operating working capital, reserving for both cash-consuming expansion and potentially temporary liquidation benefits. The construction therefore measures working-capital-realizable gross profit rather than reusing an asset-turnover trend or a standalone working-capital-growth anomaly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Productive Liability-Origin Cash Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash balances not attributable to recent liability growth are more likely to be undervalued when current-asset productivity is improving.
evaluated.reasoning: Liability-origin-adjusted cash value produced strong evidence with broad coverage, but internally sourced cash can still be idle. The separate productivity state distinguishes cash retained by improving operations from cash associated with contraction or inefficient asset accumulation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Internally Earned Cash Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when cash is neither offset by accumulated losses nor accompanied by recent liability expansion.
evaluated.reasoning: Accumulated deficits and positive liability growth represent distinct stock-based and financing-source encumbrances on apparent cash value. Keeping cash as a nonnegative numerator and placing both penalties in the denominator preserves sign consistency while requiring the discount to reflect plausibly internally earned liquidity.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Gross-Profit Claim Coverage Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when gross profit provides strong coverage of current liabilities.
evaluated.reasoning: This uses a single operating-coverage mechanism rather than blending previously evaluated cash and funding signals. The nonnegative sales-yield leg scales a signed gross-profit coverage measure, so firms with negative gross profit receive low scores while profitable firms with manageable near-term claims rank highly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stable Earned-Capital Cash Value
evaluated.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their accumulated earned-capital base is stable rather than subject to large historical revisions or swings.
evaluated.reasoning: Retained-earnings instability captures a different quality mechanism from profitability trends, accumulated deficits, or liability-funded cash provenance. Because cash and the volatility of the retained-earnings stock are both dollar stocks, the denominator treats unstable earned capital as an additional uncertainty claim on apparent cash value.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Creditor-for-Earned-Capital Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms underperform when growth in creditor claims exceeds growth in internally earned shareholder capital by a large amount relative to market value.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a continuous capital-source substitution measure rather than another cash-coverage hinge or rank ensemble. Liability and retained-earnings changes are comparable dollar-stock flows, so a high score directly identifies cheap firms replacing earned capital with creditor financing.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Maturity-Compression Asset Trap
evaluated.hypothesis: Asset-cheap firms underperform when current liabilities are becoming a persistently larger share of total liabilities.
evaluated.reasoning: The quality state is liability maturity compression rather than liability growth, cash shortfall, or operating-cost funding intensity. The nonnegative asset-to-market leg amplifies a signed migration toward near-term claims, while declining current-liability shares produce low or negative trap scores.
