considered.hypothesis: High dividend-yield firms outperform when recurring operating cash flow provides strong coverage of short-term liability claims.
considered.reasoning: This replaces retained-profit accumulation with a payout-sustainability mechanism linking market yield to cash coverage of near-term obligations. Dividend payers with negative operating cash flow receive negative scores, while zero-dividend firms remain neutral rather than being mixed into the distressed short tail.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Liquidity-Recovery Book Bargain
considered.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms outperform when their net liquid-asset position is improving relative to total assets.
considered.reasoning: Unlike the static net-net ratio, this signal uses book value for valuation and the trajectory of normalized liquidity as a separate quality state. The weak-link interaction requires both a genuine book discount and balance-sheet recovery, reducing exposure to firms that remain cheap because liquidity continues to deteriorate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Depreciation-Reconciled Earnings Value
considered.hypothesis: Firms are more likely to be genuine earnings-value bargains when the cash-versus-income difference is largely explained by depreciation rather than other accrual movements.
considered.reasoning: Depreciation is an expected noncash source of the operating-cash-flow and income gap; the remaining absolute residual captures less transparent working-capital and accrual effects. Subtracting that residual from smoothed earnings produces a conservative yield that rewards both cheapness and accounting reconciliation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Downside-Covered Operating Value
considered.hypothesis: Debt-inclusive EBITDA bargains outperform when operating cash flow has consistently covered current liabilities even in the weakest recent period.
considered.reasoning: The minimum historical cash-coverage ratio measures downside solvency rather than average profitability, helping exclude firms whose current valuation reflects episodic funding stress. The weak-link interaction requires both operating cheapness and robust claim coverage, which should produce cleaner long and short portfolio tails.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Working-Capital-Release-Adjusted Cash Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating cash flow after removing cash generated through working-capital liquidation earn stronger subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The positive-part adjustment subtracts only declines in noncash working capital that temporarily boost operating cash flow; it does not add back working-capital investment. This asymmetric treatment is conservative and avoids reconstructing the conventional cash-flow-to-price numerator.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Liability-Productivity Sales Value
considered.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when operating earnings generated per dollar of liabilities are improving.
considered.reasoning: The quality mechanism is creditor productivity rather than an arbitrarily weighted penalty for liability growth. Because sales yield is generally nonnegative, deterioration in EBITDA per liability lowers the signal directly, while improving liability productivity amplifies cheap sales without combining mismatched quantities additively.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Enterprise Earned-Cash Discount
considered.hypothesis: Cash is more likely to be undervalued when it is inexpensive relative to total capital claims and supported by accumulated internal profitability.
considered.reasoning: This retains enterprise scaling to reduce concentration in small, levered cash-rich firms but replaces the empirically weak operating-cash-flow-to-current-liabilities leg with the better-supported retained-earnings quality state. The cash ratio is nonnegative, so accumulated deficits intentionally reduce the score rather than creating a flow-driven sign inversion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Historically Restored Margin Value
considered.hypothesis: Low price-to-sales firms outperform when gross margins are both economically strong and near the top of the firm’s own recent history.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the generic book-value-plus-improving-profitability construction with a firm-specific margin-restoration mechanism. The nested weak-link interaction requires cheap sales, a strong margin level, and a favorable within-firm margin position, preventing any single textbook value or quality leg from dominating.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dual-Reserve Distributable Cash Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to cash remaining after both a replacement reserve and any working-capital liquidation benefit earn stronger subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Maintenance-adjusted cash flow and release-adjusted cash flow separately produced the strongest portfolio evidence in prior generations. This construction requires cash to survive both adjustments, targeting genuinely distributable operating cash rather than combining the two signals as separate ranked anomalies.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Claim-Adjusted Liability Productivity
considered.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales relative to total capital claims outperform when EBITDA generated per dollar of liabilities is improving.
considered.reasoning: Liability-productivity sales value produced reliable portfolio alpha but a weaker cross-sectional slope, potentially because market-cap scaling made highly levered firms appear excessively cheap. Including total liabilities in the valuation denominator retains the operational-improvement mechanism while requiring cheapness relative to all claims.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Maintenance Cash Runway Discount
considered.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms outperform when their cash discount is not offset by an ongoing maintenance-adjusted operating cash burn.
considered.reasoning: The quality penalty activates only when operating cash flow after depreciation is negative, so profitable firms retain an ordinary cash-value interpretation while cash-burning firms receive a continuous runway penalty. This asymmetric denominator avoids multiplying cash value by a signed flow and directly targets cash-rich value traps.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rising-Claims Asset Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to assets underperform when a rising share of those assets is financed by liabilities.
considered.reasoning: Assets-to-market is often elevated precisely because equity value has collapsed under creditor pressure; here that leverage sensitivity is used deliberately to identify traps rather than treated as genuine cheapness. The nonnegative asset-value leg amplifies a signed deterioration in the liability ratio, producing a directly interpretable negative-return signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Refinancing-Relief Cash Discount
considered.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when the proportion of liabilities requiring near-term settlement is declining.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the familiar cash-to-price × profitability composite with a liability-maturity mechanism: cash becomes more plausibly available to shareholders as refinancing pressure recedes. The cash-yield leg is nonnegative, so a rising current-liability share produces an intentionally negative score rather than an accidental sign inversion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Maintenance-Confirmed Sales Value
considered.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when those sales generate positive cash profitability after a depreciation-based replacement reserve.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the gross-margin family that produced strong cross-sectional slopes but no portfolio alpha and instead uses the empirically stronger maintenance-cash mechanism as the quality test. Ranking the two legs separately eliminates the scale mismatch, while the weak-link interaction prevents cheap sales from compensating for poor distributable cash generation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value
considered.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash discount is not offset by a cumulative retained-earnings deficit.
considered.reasoning: Unlike cash-to-price multiplied by a generic profitability rank, this construction treats accumulated losses as a stock claim against the apparent cash surplus. The asymmetric penalty leaves positive-retained-earnings firms on a normal cash-value scale while continuously demoting cash-rich firms with deep historical deficits.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Idle-Asset Value Trap
considered.hypothesis: Asset-cheap firms underperform when sales generated per dollar of current assets are persistently declining.
considered.reasoning: The severe portfolio failure of liquidity-recovery book value suggests that apparent balance-sheet improvement can reflect contraction or idle-asset accumulation rather than genuine quality. This signal deliberately identifies that trap by combining asset cheapness with deteriorating current-asset productivity instead of rewarding liquidity growth itself.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Operating-Asset-Liquidation-Adjusted Cash Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating cash flow after removing proceeds from noncash current-asset liquidation earn stronger subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Declines in noncash current assets, unlike generic increases in current liabilities, represent operating working-capital releases that directly elevate operating cash flow. The one-sided haircut therefore removes an identifiable liquidation benefit without incorrectly treating short-term borrowing as an operating inflow.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash-Bounded Operating Claim Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to conservatively cash-realizable operating earnings earn stronger subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: The lower of smoothed EBITDA and operating cash flow prevents reported operating earnings from exceeding their cash realization while giving no extra reward when cash flow temporarily exceeds EBITDA. Both numerator inputs are flows and the denominator is a stock of equity and liability claims, eliminating the prior flow-stock adjustment mismatch.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Retained-Earnings Rollforward Value
considered.hypothesis: High earnings-yield firms earn stronger subsequent returns when reported income reconciles with additions to retained earnings plus common dividends.
considered.reasoning: The retained-earnings rollforward provides an accounting-identity quality check rather than another profitability level or growth signal. Subtracting the absolute unexplained residual from earnings penalizes cheap firms affected by restatements, direct-to-equity adjustments, or other opaque reconciliation items; unreported dividends are treated as zero.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Capital-Consumption Asset Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to assets underperform when depreciation expense is rising persistently relative to sales.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the repeated maintenance-cash-burn aggregation with a deterioration mechanism linking asset cheapness to increasing capital consumption per revenue dollar. The nonnegative asset-value leg amplifies a signed depreciation-intensity trend, identifying assets that may look cheap because their productive economics are worsening.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accrual-Bounded Cash Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to the lower of operating cash flow and accrual-implied cash earnings earn stronger subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: Income plus depreciation provides an accrual-based cash-earnings benchmark, while reported operating cash flow captures realized cash generation. Taking the lower value prevents temporary working-capital releases from inflating the signal without requiring the sparse current-asset-change data used by earlier liquidation adjustments.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accrual-Opacity Asset Trap
considered.hypothesis: Asset-cheap firms underperform when the cash-versus-income gap contains a large component not explained by depreciation.
considered.reasoning: The prior reconciliation signal may have diluted the effect by subtracting opacity from a positive earnings yield across the full distribution. This trap-side construction instead concentrates directly on cheap assets with large absolute non-depreciation accrual residuals, creating a clean negative-return hypothesis without signed-accrual inversions.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Signed Deficit-Adjusted Cash Yield
considered.hypothesis: Positive operating cash flow predicts stronger returns when it is inexpensive and not undermined by accumulated deficits, while negative operating cash flow remains an unambiguously adverse signal.
considered.reasoning: The expression separates positive and negative cash-flow branches: deficits enlarge the denominator only for positive cash flow, while negative cash flow enters as an explicitly negative yield. This removes the prior sign reversal that made deficit-laden cash burners appear less negative and therefore artificially better ranked.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Noncash-Asset Liquidation Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms generating large noncash current-asset liquidations relative to market value earn weaker subsequent returns.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the declining-productivity template and directly measures the liquidation source that earlier conservative cash-yield signals successfully removed from operating cash flow. Scaling the one-sided liquidation amount by market value targets firms whose apparent cheapness depends materially on selling down receivables, inventory, or other operating current assets.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Short-Term Funding Sales Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to sales underperform when current liabilities are rising persistently relative to the operating costs they support.
considered.reasoning: Current liabilities are evaluated relative to cost of goods sold rather than treated as a direct offset to cash holdings, distinguishing operating funding pressure from a static cash anomaly. The nonnegative sales-yield leg amplifies a signed deterioration in short-term funding intensity without relying on unstable operating-cash-flow coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deficit-Burden Sales Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms that look inexpensive relative to sales underperform when accumulated losses represent a large share of their asset base.
considered.reasoning: Both legs are nonnegative, so deeper accumulated deficits always strengthen the trap signal and cannot improve the ranking when another component is adverse. This uses the empirically successful deficit mechanism on the trap side, identifying cheap revenue bases lacking evidence of cumulative shareholder value creation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Continuous Maintenance Sales Value
considered.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when those sales support positive maintenance-adjusted cash profitability.
considered.reasoning: The earlier MIN combination of these channels produced a poor long-short portfolio because any weak leg pushed heterogeneous firms into the short tail. This continuous interaction instead makes cash-burning firms explicitly negative and scales positive maintenance profitability by sales cheapness, preserving economically ordered tails.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EBITDA Cash-Conversion Sales Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms that look inexpensive relative to sales underperform when EBITDA materially exceeds operating cash flow relative to their operating cost base.
considered.reasoning: A positive EBITDA-to-cash shortfall identifies operating earnings that have not been realized in cash, while the one-sided operator avoids penalizing firms whose cash flow exceeds EBITDA. Scaling the shortfall by cost of goods sold makes the quality defect comparable across firms before sales cheapness magnifies it.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: EBITDA-Cash Concordance Claim Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to operating earnings earn stronger subsequent returns when EBITDA and operating cash flow are closely aligned.
considered.reasoning: The prior lower-bound claim yield penalized only cash flow below EBITDA, even though unusually high cash flow can also reflect temporary working-capital liquidation. Subtracting the absolute EBITDA-cash gap creates a symmetric realization penalty while keeping the numerator in dollar flows and the denominator in total equity and liability claims.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Working-Asset Cash Productivity Value
considered.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when their current-asset base generates high operating cash flow.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the accumulated-deficit cash-stock construction with an operating-efficiency mechanism linking sales valuation to cash productivity. The nonnegative sales-yield leg scales a signed cash-return measure, so cash-consuming firms receive negative scores rather than benefiting from a denominator adjustment.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash-Conversion Instability Sales Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to sales underperform when conversion of gross profit into operating cash flow is unstable.
considered.reasoning: This abandons working-capital growth and instead measures second-moment instability in the realization of gross profit as cash. High values require both apparent sales cheapness and unreliable cash conversion, targeting a specific trap tail rather than repackaging declining asset turnover.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Accelerating Funding-Pressure Sales Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales underperform when current liabilities relative to operating costs are increasing at an accelerating rate.
considered.reasoning: Acceleration is signed: worsening funding pressure raises the signal, while decelerating or reversing pressure lowers it, restoring the intended negative-return ordering that the nonnegative historical-rank leg lacked. It tests whether the strongest funding-pressure anomaly is concentrated in firms where short-term financing stress is intensifying rather than merely elevated.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value
considered.hypothesis: Deficit-adjusted cash bargains earn stronger subsequent returns when current-asset productivity is also improving.
considered.reasoning: The accumulated-deficit cash ratio supplies the strongest broad-coverage value evidence, while improving sales per current asset distinguishes productive liquidity from idle cash accumulation. Using separate ranked channels avoids sign reversals and does not mechanically multiply cash value by a potentially negative quality state.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding-Safe Maintenance Sales Value
considered.hypothesis: Maintenance-cash-supported sales bargains earn stronger returns when short-term funding pressure is easing rather than intensifying.
considered.reasoning: Continuous maintenance sales value generated coherent slope and portfolio evidence, while rising current liabilities relative to costs reliably identified the opposite trap tail. The ranked composite preserves both effects on comparable scales without multiplying two signed quantities or allowing worsening funding pressure to improve the score.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Maintenance-Productive Cash Discount
considered.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when ongoing operations generate positive cash profitability after a depreciation-based replacement reserve.
considered.reasoning: The cash-yield leg is nonnegative, so maintenance cash profitability determines the signal’s direction without sign inversion: cash-burning firms receive negative scores and productive firms positive scores. This tests whether the strong cash-discount and maintenance-cash mechanisms reinforce one another continuously rather than only through a distress-only denominator penalty.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when growth in current liabilities exceeds operating cash generation by a large amount relative to market value.
considered.reasoning: This measures a single funding-shortfall mechanism rather than averaging separate productivity and funding-pressure signals. The liability change and operating cash flow are both dollar flows, while market-value scaling makes the uncovered claim growth most consequential among apparently cheap firms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Through-Cycle Depreciation-Covered EBITDA Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to EBITDA earn stronger subsequent returns when operating earnings cover a conservative through-cycle depreciation burden.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the liability-productivity substitution with a capital-consumption mechanism: recent peak depreciation serves as a conservative reserve against overstated operating earning power. Firms whose smoothed EBITDA cannot cover that reserve receive low or negative yields, reducing exposure to capital-intensive value traps.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash-Covered Conservative Claim Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms earn stronger subsequent returns when conservatively cash-realizable operating earnings are inexpensive relative to equity value plus liabilities not covered by cash.
considered.reasoning: Cash modifies the economic claim base directly rather than entering as a separately ranked value signal, while the lower-bound numerator prevents EBITDA from exceeding its cash realization. The nonnegative unfunded-liability term avoids negative-enterprise-value distortions and represents the obligations that remain after available cash coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value
considered.hypothesis: Deficit-adjusted cash bargains earn stronger subsequent returns when current liabilities are declining relative to the operating costs they finance.
considered.reasoning: Rising short-term funding intensity generated strong negative cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, making its reversal an economically supported quality state rather than an untested screen. The construction combines the cash-value level with standalone funding relief, avoiding duplication of a common price-scaled value leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Liability-Origin-Adjusted Cash Value
considered.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their cash balances are not explained by recent growth in liability financing.
considered.reasoning: This tests cash provenance rather than combining cash value with another profitability measure: positive liability growth is treated as an external source that reduces the cash plausibly generated for shareholders. The cash stock and liability change are both dollar quantities, and cash raised without liability expansion retains its full valuation weight.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Through-Cycle Solvency Sales Value
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to sales earn stronger subsequent returns when current assets have consistently covered total liabilities.
considered.reasoning: The quality mechanism is a through-cycle uncovered-liability stock rather than another profitability or turnover trend. Because sales are generally nonnegative, adding the recent maximum solvency shortfall to the valuation denominator cannot create the sign reversal that occurs when denominator penalties are applied to negative earnings.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deteriorating Cash-Conversion Sales Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms that appear inexpensive relative to sales underperform when conversion of gross profit into operating cash flow is persistently deteriorating.
considered.reasoning: This targets a signed change in cash realization rather than substituting one accounting denominator inside an existing productivity formula. The nonnegative sales-yield leg magnifies worsening cash conversion among cheap firms, while improving conversion produces a negative trap score.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Double-Funding Distress Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when they simultaneously increase current liabilities and liquidate noncash current assets by amounts large relative to market value.
considered.reasoning: The minimum of the two positive-part flows requires both forms of emergency funding rather than allowing either generic working-capital movement to dominate. This identifies firms raising short-term claims while also consuming receivables, inventory, or other operating liquidity—a sharper distress mechanism than a depreciation tweak to cash-flow coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Working-Capital-Reserved Gross Profit Yield
considered.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to gross profit earn stronger subsequent returns when that profit does not require a large working-capital adjustment.
considered.reasoning: Gross profit is reduced by the absolute dollar movement in noncash operating working capital, reserving for both cash-consuming expansion and potentially temporary liquidation benefits. The construction therefore measures working-capital-realizable gross profit rather than reusing an asset-turnover trend or a standalone working-capital-growth anomaly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Productive Liability-Origin Cash Value
considered.hypothesis: Cash balances not attributable to recent liability growth are more likely to be undervalued when current-asset productivity is improving.
considered.reasoning: Liability-origin-adjusted cash value produced strong evidence with broad coverage, but internally sourced cash can still be idle. The separate productivity state distinguishes cash retained by improving operations from cash associated with contraction or inefficient asset accumulation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Internally Earned Cash Value
considered.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when cash is neither offset by accumulated losses nor accompanied by recent liability expansion.
considered.reasoning: Accumulated deficits and positive liability growth represent distinct stock-based and financing-source encumbrances on apparent cash value. Keeping cash as a nonnegative numerator and placing both penalties in the denominator preserves sign consistency while requiring the discount to reflect plausibly internally earned liquidity.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Gross-Profit Claim Coverage Value
considered.hypothesis: Firms with inexpensive sales earn stronger subsequent returns when gross profit provides strong coverage of current liabilities.
considered.reasoning: This uses a single operating-coverage mechanism rather than blending previously evaluated cash and funding signals. The nonnegative sales-yield leg scales a signed gross-profit coverage measure, so firms with negative gross profit receive low scores while profitable firms with manageable near-term claims rank highly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stable Earned-Capital Cash Value
considered.hypothesis: Cash-rich firms earn stronger subsequent returns when their accumulated earned-capital base is stable rather than subject to large historical revisions or swings.
considered.reasoning: Retained-earnings instability captures a different quality mechanism from profitability trends, accumulated deficits, or liability-funded cash provenance. Because cash and the volatility of the retained-earnings stock are both dollar stocks, the denominator treats unstable earned capital as an additional uncertainty claim on apparent cash value.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Creditor-for-Earned-Capital Trap
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when growth in creditor claims exceeds growth in internally earned shareholder capital by a large amount relative to market value.
considered.reasoning: This is a continuous capital-source substitution measure rather than another cash-coverage hinge or rank ensemble. Liability and retained-earnings changes are comparable dollar-stock flows, so a high score directly identifies cheap firms replacing earned capital with creditor financing.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Maturity-Compression Asset Trap
considered.hypothesis: Asset-cheap firms underperform when current liabilities are becoming a persistently larger share of total liabilities.
considered.reasoning: The quality state is liability maturity compression rather than liability growth, cash shortfall, or operating-cost funding intensity. The nonnegative asset-to-market leg amplifies a signed migration toward near-term claims, while declining current-liability shares produce low or negative trap scores.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: This is a near-mechanical product of two textbook anomalies (earnings yield and Sloan accruals) with no new economic content, and the multiplicative form of two rank variables is fragile — if the rank operator is zero-centered, two doubly-bad firms produce a large positive score, inverting the intended monotonicity.

This is essentially book-to-market screened on positive retained earnings, i.e., a rediscovery of the value anomaly combined with the known retained-earnings/contributed-capital decomposition, and the 0/1 indicator collapses all negative-RE firms into a single tied bucket that sits alongside genuinely low-B/M firms, muddying the sort.

EBITDA/EV and cash-flow persistence are each familiar, but the weak-link MIN operator over a cheapness rank and a joint level-plus-stability cash-profitability rank is a genuinely non-linear, economically coherent interaction whose expected positive sign matches the construction.

The hypothesis matches the expression's direction (quality-scaled sales yield), but the numerator subtracts a volatility from a level with no scaling justification and the ratio can flip sign when average margins are negative, so the interaction is coherent only over the profitable subsample.

The payout-sustainability conditioning on leverage trajectory is a defensible and reasonably novel refinement of dividend yield, but the large mass of zero-dividend firms creates ties at zero and the rank-product form shares the sign-inversion risk if ranks are zero-centered.

Assets-to-market is cheap largely *because* of leverage, so it is strongly negatively correlated with the equity-ratio leg, and the MIN operator will therefore be bound almost always by the low-leverage component — collapsing the signal into a plain balance-sheet-strength score with the value content largely arbitraged away; it also reuses the same MIN+SUMRANK(level,trend) template as the EBITDA-yield proposal.

The dominant leg is gross-profits-to-market, a well-documented published anomaly (Novy-Marx's "other side of value"), and the second leg (working capital/assets) is a weak, loosely motivated screen, so the min-combination adds only modest incremental content over a known factor.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Retained Profit Accumulation Yield (MA window 3→2, denominator ME→ME+LT) rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the resulting quantity is close to a standard earnings-to-enterprise-value ratio.

EBITDA/EV combined with a subtracted liability-growth flow is dimensionally coherent and economically motivated, though the reviewer should check that the Δliabilities term does not dominate and reduce the signal to a repackaged debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly.

(Current assets − total liabilities)/market cap is exactly Graham's net-current-asset-value (net-net) ratio, a long-published value strategy, so this is a direct rediscovery with no cross-theme content beyond a standard balance-sheet value ratio.

Economically sensible and internally consistent, but subtracting depreciation from operating cash flow largely reverses the non-cash add-back and pushes the signal toward a conventional earnings-to-price ratio, so its incremental information over E/P should be verified.

The construction is internally consistent (a nonnegative yield scaling a signed quality state, as claimed) and the cash-source distinction is a reasonable cross-theme idea, though both legs (cash-to-market, retained-earnings-to-assets) are individually known and the product will be dominated by small, cash-rich firms.

Adding back ΔNWC to OANCF simply reconstructs net income plus depreciation, so the signal collapses into the classic Lakonishok-Shleifer-Vishny cash-flow-to-price anomaly, and the stated motivation is internally inconsistent (it claims to pursue the "conservative-cash mechanism" that worked by *subtracting* depreciation, while this construction is strictly less conservative, and the coverage argument is dubious since dp is more widely reported than act/lct).

This is essentially the archived Self-Financed EBITDA Value with the liability penalty re-scaled, i.e. a cosmetic re-weighting rather than a new mechanism, and the subtraction of a dimensionless Δ(lt/at) (~0.02) from an EBITDA/EV yield (~0.10) imposes an arbitrary, uncalibrated relative weight that will be dominated by the valuation leg anyway.

The EV-scaling of cash is a sensible fix to the small/levered concentration problem, but the second leg (MA(oancf/lct)) is recycled from Claim-Covered Dividend Value, which already failed badly (fmb 0.855), and the multiplicative form is sign-unstable because negative operating cash flow flips the product and scrambles the ranking of cash-rich distressed firms.

Penalizing a smoothed earnings yield by the *absolute* non-depreciation accrual residual is a genuinely novel construction (accrual-quality-adjusted E/P rather than the signed Sloan accrual), units are internally consistent since both terms are dollar flows scaled by market cap, and it plausibly separates transparent from opaque cheapness.

The diagnosis of the failed liquidity-recovery signal is sound and the substitution of gross-profit productivity trend is economically better motivated, but "high book-to-market plus improving fundamental profitability" is close to a direct rediscovery of Piotroski's F-score value strategy and of the well-documented value-plus-quality interaction.

Replacing average coverage with a worst-case TS_MIN coverage floor is a substantively different construct (downside solvency, not mean profitability) and the weak-link form differs from the archived multiplicative Through-Cycle signal, though it is still assembled entirely from previously tested legs and a 3-year annual minimum is a noisy estimate of "worst case."

The expression correctly implements a double haircut (depreciation reserve plus the one-sided working-capital-release penalty via MAX(...,0)) and matches the stated hypothesis and positive sign, though it is essentially the intersection of two already-tested archive constructions and will inherit their thin ~0.07 coverage, so the incremental information is modest.

This is a near-mechanical variant of the archived Earned-Cash Discount with the retained-earnings stock swapped for its own already-tested flow (Retained Profit Accumulation Yield), and since Δre/at is essentially dividend-net ROA the signal reduces to the familiar cash-to-price × profitability composite rather than a new mechanism.

The revision is diagnostically motivated (rescaling cheapness to all claims to defuse the leverage artifact behind the weak FMB slope) and sign-consistent, but placing lt in both the valuation denominator and the productivity trend creates a mechanical shared-denominator interaction that could confound interpretation of any improvement.

The added VOL(oancf/at,3) term is one to two orders of magnitude smaller than typical price-to-sales values, so the denominator is dominated by P/S and the signal collapses to margin × sales-yield — a rediscovery of the archived Durable Margin Sales Value and Through-Cycle Margin Floor Value that already produced zero portfolio alpha.

The one-sided burn penalty is internally consistent, dimensionally sound (dollars added to dollars), and preserves the intended positive sign, but because maintenance-adjusted burn is small relative to market cap for most firms the adjustment will only re-rank a distressed minority, limiting expected incremental power over plain cash-to-price.

The construction is internally coherent — a nonnegative assets-to-market leg amplifies a signed change in liability share, so the short leg is levering-up asset-cheap firms and the long leg deleveraging ones, consistent with the negative expected sign — and it explores a genuinely different (trap-side) direction than the archive, with the main caveat that Δ(lt/at) overlaps the known debt-issuance/leverage-change anomaly and the value-leg component pulls in the opposite direction.

This is a narrower re-cut of the already-tested Working-Capital-Release-Adjusted Cash Yield, and it is internally inconsistent because lct includes debt in current liabilities and notes payable whose increases never enter oancf, so the haircut penalizes financing inflows that were never counted in the numerator.

The denominator adds a one-year liability *flow* to a market-cap *stock*, a dimensional mismatch that makes the adjustment negligible for most firms so the signal collapses into a plain change-in-earnings-to-price measure — essentially the already-tested Retained Profit Accumulation Yield template and a well-known earnings-growth-to-price anomaly.

The one-sided stock-based deficit penalty is economically distinct from the earlier flow-burn and multiplicative-profitability versions of cash-to-price, and the sign logic is coherent, though it reuses the archive's che/(mktcap + max(penalty,0)) template closely enough that incremental information over Earned-Cash Discount is uncertain.

TREND(cogs/sale) is mechanically the negative of the gross-margin trend, so this is the sign-flipped mirror of the archive's sales-yield × margin-quality family (Durable Margin, Through-Cycle Margin Floor) and adds little beyond a known gross-margin-trend value interaction.

This is a pure parameter/aggregation tweak of Maintenance Cash Runway Discount (MA over 2 → TS_SUM over 3 of the identical oancf−dp burn), i.e., a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Sign logic is internally consistent and the deteriorating-turnover trap leg is economically distinct from the failed leverage-change leg of Rising-Claims Asset Trap, though it reuses that same at/mktcap × trend template and the choice of current assets rather than total assets as the turnover base is unmotivated.

The deficit penalty is sign-inconsistent when applied to a numerator that can be negative — inflating the denominator makes loss-making, deficit-laden firms' cash-flow yields *less* negative and therefore rank *higher*, exactly reversing the intended trap-avoidance mechanism that worked when the numerator was always-positive cash (che).

This is a cosmetic respecification of the archived Idle-Asset Value Trap (same at/mktcap × NEG(TREND(productivity)) template with sale/act swapped for gross-profit/at), and the productivity leg alone is close to a known declining-gross-profitability signal.

The min(oancf, ib+dp) construction is internally coherent and correctly implements the stated conservatism (it binds precisely when working-capital releases inflate cash flow), though it is structurally close to the archived Cash-Bounded Operating Claim Yield and the base leg is essentially the classic cash-flow-to-price anomaly.

A two-variable stock ratio with no genuine cross-theme interaction that essentially rediscovers the well-documented cash-holdings/net-cash-to-price anomaly, and it sits adjacent to the archived Enterprise Earned-Cash Discount family.

This mechanically bolts the deficit denominator from one archived signal onto the archived Liability-Productivity Sales Value expression, and the adjustment misfires in the same direction problem: when the EBITDA/liability trend is negative, shrinking the valuation leg for deficit firms makes the product *less* negative and thus ranks the worst firms higher.

The expression is internally consistent with the stated negative sign (cheap assets × large unexplained accrual magnitude), and the absolute-value opacity framing is a defensible departure from the weak signed reconciliation predecessor, though it overlaps conceptually with known accrual-quality/earnings-opacity effects and the multiplicative scaling makes the value leg mostly a magnitude amplifier.

This is essentially an algebraic reparameterization of the archive's already-tested "Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value" (moving the deficit from denominator to numerator), which will be very highly correlated with it and constitutes a cosmetic rather than substantive variant.

The diagnosis of why the earlier MIN-combination failed is sound and the continuous product creates economically ordered tails, though it remains a value×quality composite in the same family as the previously weak sales-yield interaction signals.

GROWTH(act−che) minus GROWTH(sale) is arithmetically the declining noncash-current-asset turnover the proposal claims not to reuse, making it a near-duplicate of the archived "Idle-Asset Value Trap" and, more broadly, of the well-known accruals/working-capital-growth anomaly.

Internally consistent and the one-sided truncation is well motivated, but ebitda−oancf embeds cash interest and taxes, so the "unrealized earnings" leg partly proxies for leverage and tax burden rather than accrual quality, and the value×accruals combination is close to established anomaly territory.

TS_RANK is strictly non-negative, so unlike the TREND version the product can never push cheap firms into the short tail and the composite becomes a monotone rescaling of the sales-yield value signal — which implies a positive slope, directly contradicting the stated negative expected sign.

The symmetric-penalty motivation is a genuine economic distinction from the archived lower-bound claim yield, but ebitda−oancf is dominated by cash interest and taxes rather than accrual misalignment, so the "concordance" interpretation of the numerator is only loosely supported by what the expression actually computes.

This is a mechanical equal-weight rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals (Idle-Asset Value Trap and Short-Term Funding Sales Trap) whose legs share a common price-scaled cheapness component, so it is an ensemble rather than a new mechanism and will almost surely land between the two parent results.

Pairing the archive's strongest value leg with a genuinely untested standalone current-asset productivity trend is defensible and avoids sign-inversion from multiplying a signed quality term, but the 50/50 rank weighting hands half the signal to a leg with no standalone evidence and risks diluting the parent's alpha.

Combining maintenance-cash-supported sales value with an independently ranked (rather than multiplied) easing-funding-pressure leg is a coherent construction and the sign logic is internally consistent, though it is close in spirit to the previous proposal and its incremental information over the archived parent is likely modest.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived Liability-Productivity Sales Value, differing only by replacing lt with lct in the denominator of the EBITDA-productivity trend, which is exactly the kind of superficial substitution the objective warns against.

Swapping the flow-based maintenance cash margin for the stock-based retained-earnings term in the archived Earned-Cash Discount is a modest but economically motivated change, and the stated sign logic (nonnegative cash yield leg, direction set by the quality term) correctly matches what the expression computes — though it remains a recombination of two well-worn archive components.

A direct rank-sum of two already-evaluated archive signals with no new economic content; blending a t_alpha 1.81 signal with a t_alpha 2.88 signal is portfolio bookkeeping, not a test of a distinct mechanism.

This is the archive's Maintenance-Productive Cash Discount with a single denominator tweak (adding the retained-earnings deficit already tested in Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value), so it is a near-collinear cosmetic merger of two existing signals rather than a new mechanism, even though the construction is internally consistent and the nonnegativity argument is correct.

It re-specifies the identical two legs of the archive's best signal (Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value) as a raw product instead of a rank sum, which adds no new economic content and introduces a scale-domination problem because a small-magnitude TREND(sale/act) is multiplied by a fat-tailed cash-yield level.

Swapping sale for ebitda in the productivity-trend leg of an already-evaluated SUMRANK signal is a mechanical ingredient substitution likely to be highly correlated with the original (and the turnover/margin decomposition it invokes is essentially published DuPont-component evidence), so the incremental information is small.

This is a genuinely new pairing of two independently supported legs (deficit-adjusted cash yield and easing short-term funding intensity) with no shared price-scaled denominator and a sign that matches the expression's direction, though it reuses a familiar SUMRANK template and the funding-relief leg has only been validated interacted with sales yield.

Economically coherent and correctly signed, but it differs from the archive's Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap by a single dp term inside the same hinge, which will mostly shift the truncation threshold and produce a signal nearly collinear with the one already tested.

This is the mirror image of the already-evaluated Idle-Asset Value Trap within a sales-yield × trend template that the archive has mined repeatedly with weak results, and because sale appears in both factors the "interaction" is partly mechanical rather than a clean value-times-quality conjunction; the turnover-change component also closely tracks published asset-turnover (DuPont) return predictability.

This is a mechanical blend of two already-tested archive winners (Productive Deficit-Adjusted Cash Value and Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value) that share an identical cash leg, so it is a re-weighting exercise whose result is largely predictable from the correlation of the two parents rather than a new mechanism.

The cash-provenance leg (cash net of recent liability expansion) and the current-asset productivity leg are economically distinct and non-overlapping, and the construction is sign-consistent with broad coverage, though it is a template substitution on a prior composite rather than a genuinely new mechanism.

The numerator already penalizes recent total-liability growth, so the NEG(TREND(lct/cogs)) leg substantially double-counts short-term funding expansion, and the overall form is a one-component swap into the archived Funding-Safe Deficit Cash Value template.

Folding both the deficit and the liability-growth penalty into the denominator is a coherent, sign-consistent single-ratio alternative to the two archived adjustments (multiplicative shrinkage rather than subtraction), which is a real structural difference, though the incremental information over the existing deficit-adjusted cash yield may be modest.

This is a single-input substitution (DELTA(che) for oancf) into the archived Cash-Uncovered Claim Growth Trap, and DELTA(che) is a weaker coverage proxy since cash can rise from financing or asset sales, making it partly a rediscovery of the liability-growth/working-capital accrual anomaly.

Multiplying two one-sided truncated legs (whose components are both already in the archive, one of them weak) leaves a large mass of exact zeros so the cross-sectional rank degenerates into ties over most of the universe, making any apparent improvement over the parent trap hard to attribute to the added conditioning.
